supporting_observations.claim: The alerted connections recur at roughly five-minute intervals and are attributed by endpoint network telemetry to the same GradeBook Pro updater process running as raul.diaz. Examples include connections at 13:43:25, 13:48:50, 13:54:01, 13:58:42, 14:03:12, and 14:08:35 UTC.

The updater’s connections go through the explicit proxy to update.gradebookpro.co. The supplied inventory describes the approved GradeBook Pro updater as checking update.gradebookpro.com, so the observed hostname differs from the inventory hostname.

The updater ran from raul.diaz’s AppData\Local directory, rather than the Program Files location given in the supplied inventory. A file-creation event also names that same updater executable shortly after it starts.

The first logged updater connection to the observed hostname returned proxy status 502; later connections to that hostname returned status 200. This is consistent with recurring updater activity but does not establish that the destination or executable is legitimate.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnel metadata, but the supplied records do not expose the HTTPS request or response contents, certificate details, or downloaded payload. For example, the updater tunnels are logged in T295-00172, T295-00208, and T295-00215.
The records identify the updater by path and process ID, but provide no hash, signature-validation result, or file contents for that executable (T295-00136, T295-00142).
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish whether update.gradebookpro.co is controlled by the approved GradeBook Pro vendor or is an unauthorized lookalike.
The evidence does not establish whether the AppData updater is a legitimate installation, an unauthorized copy, or a modified executable.
The tunnel byte counts and status codes do not establish what data was exchanged or whether an update was downloaded or executed (T295-00172, T295-00208, T295-00215).
The evidence does not establish that the alerted activity was malicious or that it was benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the updater executable and verify its hash, digital signature, provenance, and relationship to the approved GradeBook Pro installation.
Confirm with the software owner or vendor whether update.gradebookpro.co is an authorized update endpoint; compare DNS and TLS certificate information if available.
Collect proxy or endpoint telemetry that can establish the HTTPS request and response details and whether any downloaded content was written or executed.
Check GradeBook Pro installation and update history on WS-RDIAZ-01 to determine why the updater runs from AppData rather than the inventory-listed Program Files location.
unrelated_findings: The Cisco AnyConnect VPN UI was launched by raul.diaz, despite the supplied environment context stating there is no VPN. The records show the UI and a signed Cisco module load, but do not show a VPN connection; handle separately from this alert (T295-00318, T295-00320).

The proxy initiated an HTTP connection to WS-RDIAZ-01 on port 8530 near the end of the review window. Its purpose is not established by these records; investigate separately from the periodic outbound HTTPS alert (T295-00396, T295-00397, T295-00398).
